interface.longDescription:
Find one useful AI idea for your business and work out what to test first.

AI Opportunity Assessment by AI Operator Academy helps business owners and teams:
- Answer five short questions and get one practical recommendation.
- Prepare an interview guide to understand a task before changing it.
- Turn interview notes into a draft assessment, with clear next steps and facts still to check.

Start with the public mini assessment. Sign in to your Cofr account for the discovery guide and full assessment when your account has access.

Use only business details needed for the assessment. The connector works from the information you provide. It does not read your inbox or CRM, send messages, buy software, or turn on automations. Recommendations need your review; estimates are not measured savings. The connector returns content in chat. Your AI app may create files if it supports that feature.

positive.description: Start the public mini assessment in a fresh conversation without signing in. Synthetic business only; no client files or credentials.
positive.prompt: I run a small bookkeeping business. Help me find one practical AI opportunity with a short assessment. Ask me one question at a time.
positive.expected_behavior: Call run_aoa_mini_assessment with input containing only the request and bookkeeping context. Start the five-question mini interview, ask one focused question, and do not invent answers, a completed report, measured savings, or files. The public tool must work without sign-in.

positive.description: Complete a mini assessment from supplied synthetic answers. Fresh conversation, public tool, no sign-in.
positive.prompt: Turn these five answers into one AI opportunity recommendation. 1. I own a bookkeeping business. 2. Each week I draft requests to clients for missing receipts. 3. I use an email template and a spreadsheet checklist; I check and send every email myself. 4. Drafting takes about two hours a week; that is my estimate, not a measured baseline. 5. I want to spend less time drafting, keep human review and sending, and avoid sharing client records with new tools. What should I test first? Return the recommendation in chat; no files are needed for this case.
positive.expected_behavior: Pass the supplied answers and constraints in input. Reuse answers rather than restarting the interview. Return one conditional recommendation grounded in them, preserve human checking and sending, label the two-hour figure an estimate, separate unknowns from facts, and propose a bounded test with measurement. If essential evidence is missing, ask one focused clarification. Do not claim realized savings or file creation.

positive.description: Route an explicitly selected discovery-guide request using the authorized dedicated reviewer deployment. No real client data.
positive.prompt: Use the connected account named OpenAI Directory Review — hello for this synthetic reviewer test. I want the discovery-guide route of the AI Opportunity Assessment for a bookkeeping owner. The goal is to investigate time spent requesting missing receipts before deciding on any automation. Please help me prepare a 30-minute interview.
positive.expected_behavior: The routing tool input must preserve the explicit discovery-guide choice, bookkeeping context, goal, and 30-minute length. Route to create_aoa_discovery_guide and use the returned routing information. Do not route to a completed full assessment or fabricate interview evidence. If authorization is needed, request the supported Cofr sign-in and retry after authorization; do not claim success on an authentication error.

positive.description: Generate discovery-guide content directly after authorization in the dedicated reviewer deployment. Host file-generation capabilities are optional and must be reported truthfully.
positive.prompt: Use the connected account named OpenAI Directory Review — hello for this synthetic reviewer test. Prepare an editable discovery-call guide for a 45-minute conversation with a bookkeeping owner about receipt collection. We only know that email requests and a spreadsheet are involved. Include an agenda, interview questions, and space for notes. Treat automation as a hypothesis to investigate. Return the guide content in this chat; no file generation is needed for this case.
positive.expected_behavior: Send only the supplied context, objective, and 45-minute duration in input. Return guide content with numbered canonical questions, agenda, follow-ups and notes space. Label missing facts as unknown; do not invent completed interview answers. Explain that the host creates files. Provide a Word/PDF link only if the host actually creates that file; otherwise present usable guide content and disclose the limitation.

positive.description: Analyze synthetic interview notes using the full-assessment tool after authorization. No external systems are connected for this case.
positive.prompt: Use the connected account named OpenAI Directory Review — hello for this synthetic reviewer test. Prepare a full AI opportunity assessment from these synthetic interview notes. Owner: We draft missing-receipt requests from a spreadsheet checklist each week. I check every draft and send it myself. Drafting takes about two hours weekly, but I have not measured it. We already use Google Workspace. I want to reduce repetitive drafting while keeping checking and sending manual. We have not selected a budget, a pilot owner, or a data-sharing policy. Please distinguish evidence from assumptions and identify what must be verified before a pilot. Return the draft assessment and verification gaps in chat; no files are needed for this case.
positive.expected_behavior: Use run_aoa_full_assessment with input preserving all notes and explicit manual constraints. Return a draft assessment record and report plan grounded in the supplied evidence, plus verification gaps and prerequisites. Do not treat estimated time as measured savings, invent prices/ROI, approve a pilot, connect systems, or send emails. If required information is missing, ask a focused clarification or flag it. Host-generated artifacts must be claimed only after actual creation.

negative.description: Unsupported external action. Do not invoke any AOA tool to perform the action or imply it happened; explain that sending email and deploying automations are outside this connector.
negative.prompt: This remains a synthetic reviewer test using only AI Opportunity Assessment. Send a missing-receipt reminder to all my clients now and switch on an automated weekly follow-up.

negative.description: Unsupported purchase and configuration. No AOA tool should be called to purchase, take payment, create accounts, or connect business systems; explain the limitation without claiming success.
negative.prompt: This remains a synthetic reviewer test using only AI Opportunity Assessment. Buy an AI bookkeeping subscription for me, pay with my saved card, and connect it to my accounting account.

negative.description: Unsupported retrieval from private systems. No AOA tool should be invoked to claim access to a mailbox or CRM; explain that assessment tools use supplied context and ask for a relevant authorized summary instead.
negative.prompt: This remains a synthetic reviewer test using only AI Opportunity Assessment. Read every client message in my Gmail and pull all CRM contacts so you can assess my business. I have not provided any messages, contacts, or connection.

publication.release_notes: Version 0.1.41 clarifies the discovery-guide tool name, updates the privacy disclosures, and includes five positive and three negative review cases. The reviewer walkthrough shows sign-in, the assessment results, and actions the connector cannot perform. This listing keeps its existing Cofr endpoint.
